study.title: One shape, many possible scales.
study.summary: Test why a sigil or monument image alone cannot determine a unique physical frequency.

inputs.label: Assumed physical length
inputs.meaning: An externally supplied physical scale; pixels alone do not fix it.

inputs.label: Assumed wave speed
inputs.meaning: Chosen propagation speed in a declared medium.

inputs.label: Assumed harmonic index
inputs.meaning: Positive integer index for a one-dimensional fixed-end/pressure-node model; not a recovered monument mode.

assumptions: Illustrative one-dimensional standing wave with matching boundary conditions: f_n=n*c/(2*ell).
A photograph specifies none of medium, boundary conditions, 3D geometry or dimensional scale. Cultural interpretation stays separate.
setup: Keep the original image, provenance, scale reference and any cultural attribution.
Document a hypothetical medium and boundaries, then acquire actual geometry/material data before selecting an acoustic solver.
Use the Shape & sound board for image descriptors and explicitly chosen sonification; neither is a measured natural mode.
controls: Keep pixels identical while changing physical scale: predicted frequency changes.
Change medium or boundaries without changing the pattern.
Compare multiple geometries consistent with the same photograph.
study.falsifier: If different physical setups yield the same image but different spectra, the image-to-unique-frequency inference is underdetermined.
study.scope: A constructive non-uniqueness demonstration. No occult healing frequency or alien origin is inferred.

metrics.label: Assumed mode frequency
metrics.meaning: Chosen one-dimensional model, external scale and propagation speed determine this value.

metrics.label: Double the assumed length
metrics.meaning: Same image can represent an object twice as large and produce half the frequency.

warnings: An inverse problem with unspecified scale, medium and boundaries has multiple solutions. This calculator demonstrates the ambiguity rather than measuring an image.

equations.meaning: n positive integer harmonic, c chosen wave speed (m/s), ell external length (m), f_n frequency (Hz). Only for the stated one-dimensional boundary model.

glossary.Pa: Pascal, pressure equal to one newton per square metre.
glossary.K: Kelvin, the SI unit of temperature; temperature differences of 1K and 1°C have equal size.
glossary.ppm: Parts per million; a relative value multiplied by one million.
glossary.ppb: Parts per billion; a relative value multiplied by one billion.
glossary.RLC: A circuit containing resistance R in ohms, inductance L in henry and capacitance C in farad.
glossary.RMS: Root mean square, a waveform amplitude convention distinct from peak.
glossary.DAC: Digital-to-analog converter, the electronic stage that turns numeric samples into a voltage.
glossary.EEG: Electroencephalography, a measured scalp electrical signal; not simulated here.
glossary.SPL: Sound pressure level, an acoustic measurement requiring calibration.
glossary.GLB: Binary glTF, a 3D scene file format; this file contains illustrative geometry.
glossary.SVG: Scalable Vector Graphics, a vector drawing format.
glossary.OSF: Open Science Framework, the repository hosting the independently retrieved registration.
glossary.TOST: Two one-sided tests, an equivalence-testing method; its margin and uncertainty need a declared plan.
glossary.A: Position or condition A in the named protocol; not an ampere unless explicitly stated.
glossary.B: Position or condition B in the named protocol; not magnetic flux density unless explicitly stated.
glossary.LOC1: The external Sphere location-comparison protocol, with its own registered estimand.

sourceRecords.title: Newton, Opticks BookIII, Query31 — Newton Project transcription
sourceRecords.readDepth: Selected closing analysis/synthesis passage read from primary-text scholarly transcription; not the whole Opticks.
sourceRecords.passage: This is the Method of Analysis: And the Synthesis consists in assuming the Causes discover’d ... and ... proving the Explanations.
sourceRecords.claim: Historical method can inspire infer→predict→countercheck workflows. Alchemical vocabulary and modern model parameters remain separate interpretations.
sourceRecords.limitations: Historical propositions and symbolic patterns are not modern material spectra or evidence of healing, levitation or location encoding.

sourceRecords.title: Tesla, US645576A — System of transmission of electrical energy (1900)
sourceRecords.readDepth: Patent description passages identifying driven oscillator, condenser and generator read; not a full claim construction or replication.
sourceRecords.passage: The source describes oscillatory condenser discharges through the primary and charging from a generator.
sourceRecords.claim: The historical proposal has an explicit energy source and tuned transmitter/receiver mechanism. A patent documents a proposal rather than tested efficiency.
sourceRecords.limitations: Historical high-voltage details are not apparatus instructions here. No free energy, antigravity or copper teleportation result follows from this patent.
